The original review set's observation (Summary sheet) still holds for those 43 papers. The added sources qualify it in three ways:
1) In-the-wild GNSS interference against aircraft is now documented in peer-reviewed venues (Felux et al. 2024, NAVIGATION; Felux et al. 2025, CyCon), not only in industry and regulator material.

2) L4 (governance & integration) is no longer empty: Viasat KA-SAT (2022) is a real-world L4-to-L1 compromise, and the Black Hat 2025 disclosures add 45 verified CVEs in ground C2, flight software and the SDLS library. No source enters at L3: processing is reached only by propagation from L1/L2 (e.g. MLAT verification bypass, spoofed downlinks).
3) Top-down timing failures are real (GPS UTC error 2016, Galileo outage 2019): the cross-cutting timing dependency can fail from L4 without any attacker.
